H7014.d: Kajin, the name of the first child, also of a place in Palestine, and of an Oriental tribe
fb: Man living at the time before the Flood

Adam and Eve's firstborn, a farmer. God accepted his brother Abel's offering and not his, and Cain killed Abel out of jealousy. God marked him and sent him off to wander rather than putting him to death.

H7069.d: to erect, i.e. create; by extension, to procure, especially by purchase (causatively, sell); by implication to own

H7093.d: an extremity; adverbially (with prepositional prefix) after

fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs

Two men in the genealogies. One descends from Seth several generations before Noah; the other is a son of Arphaxad in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, a name missing from the Genesis Hebrew text but present in the Greek.

H7064.d: a nest (as fixed), sometimes including the nestlings; figuratively, a chamber or dwelling

H7043.d: to be (causatively, make) light, literally (swift, small, sharp, etc.) or figuratively (easy, trifling, vile, etc.)

H7019.d: harvest (as the crop), whether the product (grain or fruit) or the (dry) season

H7017.d: a Kenite or member of the tribe of Kajin
fb: They were a wandering clan close to Midian, outside the twelve tribes but mostly friendly to Israel. Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, was a Kenite priest, and Jael, Heber the Kenite's wife, killed Sisera.

H7074.d: a Kenizzite or descendant of Kenaz
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Caleb, one of the two spies who stayed faithful, is called a Kenizzite. The clan came from Kenaz and was tied to Edom in Genesis, then folded into Judah.
Named once, in Genesis, and nowhere else.

H7055.d: Kemuel, the name of a relative of Abraham, and of two Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 3 men called Kemuel. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
A tribal leader of Ephraim, appointed to help divide the land under Joshua.
Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Nahor's son, and so Abraham's nephew.

H7065.d: to be (causatively, make) zealous, i.e. (in a bad sense) jealous or envious

H7075.d: creation, i.e. (concretely) creatures; also acquisition, purchase, wealth

H7073.d: Kenaz, the name of an Edomite and of two Israelites
fb: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
One of Edom's clan chiefs, in Genesis 36 and again in Chronicles. The Kenizzites are counted among the Edomite clans.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Caleb's younger brother, and father of Othniel, Israel's first judge.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 3 men called Kenaz. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.

H7070.d: a reed (as erect); by resemblance a rod (especially for measuring), shaft, tube, stem, the radius (of the arm), beam (of a steelyard)

H7087.d: to shrink, i.e. thicken (as unracked wine, curdled milk, clouded sky, frozen water)

H7054.d: something that rises, i.e. a stalk of grain

H7050.d: a sling; also a (door) screen (as if slung across), or the valve (of the door) itself

H7023.d: a wall (as built in a trench)

H7033.d: to toast, i.e. scorch partially or slowly

H7096.d: to cut off; (figuratively) to destroy; (partially) to scrape off

H7081.d: a lot; also divination (including its fee), oracle

H7079.d: Kenath, a place East of the Jordan
fb: In Bashan, east of the Jordan, taken when Israel moved in and renamed Nobah after the man who took it. It is generally identified with Qanawat on the slopes of Jebel Hauran, where Roman ruins still stand, a theatre among them.

H7092.d: to draw together, i.e. close; by implication, to leap (by contracting the limbs); specifically, to die (from gathering up the feet)

H7080.d: properly, to distribute, i.e. determine by lot or magical scroll; by implication, to divine

H7034.d: to be light (as implied in rapid motion), but figuratively, only (be [causatively, hold] in contempt)

fb: Far south in Judah, near the border with Edom, in the dry country below Beersheba.
David saved this walled town from a Philistine raid while Saul was hunting him. Then he learned they would have handed him over if Saul came, and he moved on into the wilderness of Ziph.

H7071.d: Kanah, the name of a stream and of a place in Palestine
fb: The name means reedy, and this one is a stream on the border between Ephraim and Manasseh, running from the hill country to the Mediterranean. Another Kanah, a town up in Asher, is a separate place.
Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.
It was a town allotted to Zebulun. It may be Kitron, one of the places where Zebulun never drove out the Canaanites, though nobody is sure of the site.
Zebulun never drove out the Canaanites of this town, so they stayed on as forced labour, and Joshua 19:15 probably lists it as Kattath.

It is a winter stream that drains the Jezreel Valley into the Mediterranean below Mount Carmel, and it floods fast. It swept away Sisera's chariots when Deborah and Barak fought the Canaanites, and in its valley Elijah had the prophets of Baal killed after the contest on Carmel.

H7056.d: Kamon, a place East of the Jordan
fb: Jair was buried here, the judge who led Israel for twenty-two years. Where it was is disputed: tradition puts it in Gilead east of the Jordan, or else near Mount Carmel.

H7049.d: to sling; also to carve (as if a circular motion, or into light forms)

H7027.d: Kish, the name of five Israelites
fb: Saul's father living at the time of United Monarchy
Saul's father, a Benjamite of some standing. He lost his donkeys, sent Saul to find them, and the search ended with Samuel anointing Saul as Israel's first king.
Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
He is a Levite, not Saul's father. His sons married their cousins because their uncle died with only daughters, and the temple rota in Chronicles counts his family.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 4 men called Kish. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return, and Esther is the only book that names him.

H7015.d: a dirge (as accompanied by beating the breasts or on instruments)

H7095.d: shape (as if cut out); base (as if there cut off)

H7025.d: Kir-Cheres or Kir-Chareseth, a place in Moab
fb: Moab's fortress capital, modern Kerak in Jordan. When Mesha of Moab rebelled after Ahab died, Israel, Judah and Edom besieged him there, and he sacrificed his own son on the wall, which ended the siege. His own account of the revolt survives on the Moabite Stone, found in 1868.

H7024.d: Kir, a place in Assyrian; also one in Moab
fb: Amos says God brought the Arameans from Kir the way he brought Israel out of Egypt, and he warns that Damascus will be sent back there. Tiglath-pileser III did exactly that in 732 BC, and his own annals record it. Isaiah's Kir, set beside Elam in a scene of soldiers arming, may or may not be the same place.
Named once, in Isaiah, and nowhere else.
Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Kishi, or Kushaiah, was the Merarite Levite whose son Ethan was one of the three chief musicians David put to serve before the ark.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Ancestor of a family of temple servants, the Nethinim, who came back from Babylon with Zerubbabel.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
He was a Levite who had married a foreign wife and agreed under Ezra to send her away. He is also called Kelita, and is probably the Kelita who helped people understand the reading of the law.

H7042.d: Kelita, the name of three Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
The law was read out in public, and he was one of the Levites who explained it to the people. He also signed the covenant renewal under Nehemiah.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return. Ezra names him once.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
He was a priest in Joiakim's time, head of the family of Sallai, in a list of priestly family heads.

H7009.d: an opponent (as rising against one), i.e. (collectively) enemies

H7077.d: to nestle, i.e. build or occupy as a nest

H7090.d: a species of bird, perhaps the bittern (from its contracted form)

H7091.d: spring forward; an arrow-snake (as darting on its prey)

H7083.d: properly, a cup, i.e. an ink-stand

H7001.d: a knot (as tied up), i.e. (figuratively) a riddle; also a vertebra (as if a knot)
